visual_review.finding: The new brown folded-leaf and deadwood silhouettes add subtle irregular structure to previously uninterrupted near-bank ground. The change is visible but modest; blocky adult canopy, smooth broad terrain, sparse continuous litter coverage, and broad flat-looking water still dominate the scene.

accepted_findings: The regenerated L_UpperHuacas map remains reference-runnable and contains four tagged, non-colliding forest-floor HISM actors with exactly 3,300 accepted instances.
Two folded-leaf forms contribute 2,600 instances, while one buttress-root form and one deadwood form contribute 350 instances each.
All placements retain source-Landscape grounding, dry-height, slope, complete-visible-water-width, full-centerline, and protected-solver-strip screening.
All four meshes are opaque, project-owned solid geometry using the existing Pacuare Default Lit vertex-color material and Nanite.
Terrain, collision, water, cooked solver fields, hydraulics, bathymetry, buoyancy, raft forces, and exact ecology authority remain unchanged.
The final editor build, six native Pacuare tests, all six runnable-map loads, and every map's MapCheck pass.
remaining_photoreal_defects: Adult canopy crowns, trunks, branches, shrubs, and remaining procedural ground cover are angular, repetitive, and visibly synthetic.
The new forms are procedural visual gap fill and have not been accepted as Pacuare species, ecology, geology, wetness, disturbance, age, density, or seasonal evidence.
Leaf-litter coverage remains discontinuous and lacks a continuous layered forest-floor material response, decomposition, wetness, occlusion, vines, epiphytes, and small plants.
Buttress roots are scattered presentation forms rather than roots integrated into reviewed trunk bases and source-grounded tree architecture.
Broad smooth banks and the 30 m source context still lack surveyed breaklines, sub-meter microtopography, exposed rock structure, boulders, waterfalls, and rapid-scale gorge detail.
The foreground river remains broad and flat-looking with incomplete overturning wave volume, aeration, foam, spray, mist, refraction, rock-contact plumes, and shoreline transitions.
Atmospheric depth, rainy-season lighting, cloud response, wind, canopy motion, and coherent wet-surface variation remain incomplete.
The environment-only frames do not validate raft, crew, paddle, water-occlusion, guide-line, hazard, rescue, or close-range interaction quality.
No measured desktop or VR performance profile has accepted the added instance and Nanite cost on named target hardware.
required_external_acceptance_gates: A qualified Pacuare rafting guide accepts Upper Huacas route identity, water levels, entry and exit, named hazards, guide lines, rescue routes, and gameplay sightlines in runnable guide-eye views.

A geospatial reviewer accepts coordinate transforms, vertical datum, route stationing, shoreline and bank breaklines, higher-resolution terrain, rocks, waterfalls, and the declared boundary between sourced terrain and procedural gap fill.

A hydraulic reviewer accepts calibrated and converged flow bands against observed Upper Huacas discharge, surface elevations, velocities, Froude behavior, rapid-specific features, and hazard response.

A regional ecologist and environment-art reviewer accepts species and morphology analog use, density, age classes, season, wetness, disturbance, geology, ground cover, lighting, and rainforest atmosphere.

A water-VFX and character/equipment art review accepts water transmission, raft and crew occlusion, waves, holes, rollers, aeration, spray, foam, bank intersections, paddles, animation, and close-range asset quality.

Measured full-run desktop and VR profiles pass release frame-time, memory, streaming, shader, collision, capsize, recovery, stability, comfort, and complete-run gameplay budgets on named target hardware.
